title: Solving Linear Equations
subject: Mathematics
subtopic: Solving linear equations step by step

scenes.heading: Solving Linear Equations
scenes.narration: Welcome to part three of our algebra series. In this lesson we solve linear equations step by step, and check our answers.

scenes.heading: What is an equation?
bullets: An equation says that two expressions are equal
Solving means finding the value of the variable that makes it true
Whatever you do to one side, do to the other side
scenes.narration: An equation says that two expressions are equal. Solving an equation means finding the value of the variable that makes it true. Think of a balance scale: whatever you do to one side, you must do to the other side, so it stays balanced.

scenes.heading: Example 1
scenes.narration: Solve x plus seven equals twelve. To get x on its own, subtract seven from both sides. That leaves x equals five.

scenes.heading: Example 2
scenes.narration: Solve three x minus four equals eleven. Add four to both sides: three x equals fifteen. Now divide both sides by three. So x equals five.

scenes.heading: Example 3: Variables on both sides
scenes.narration: Solve five x plus two equals two x plus fourteen. Move the x terms to the left and the numbers to the right. When a term changes sides, its sign changes. So five x minus two x equals fourteen minus two. That gives three x equals twelve, and x equals four.

scenes.heading: Example 4: With brackets
scenes.narration: Solve two times, x minus three, equals ten. First expand the bracket: two x minus six equals ten. Add six to both sides: two x equals sixteen. Divide by two: x equals eight.

scenes.heading: Check your answer
scenes.narration: Always check your answer. Substitute x equals eight into the left hand side: two times, eight minus three, is two times five, which is ten. The right hand side is ten. Both sides are equal, so x equals eight is correct.

scenes.heading: Tips
bullets: Get the variable terms on one side and the numbers on the other
Check by substituting your answer into the original equation
scenes.narration: To sum up: expand any brackets first. Get the variable terms on one side and the numbers on the other side. Then divide, and always check by substituting your answer into the original equation.
